thesis: Best balance of operating progress and price strength in this group.
new_evidence: Q1 revenue grew 15.7% and EBITDA margin reached 14.8%. The company reports completed HAM monetisation, and October brings a Delhi–Saharanpur completion certificate. These are execution/capital-recycling milestones, beyond order announcements.
risk: FY26 consolidated operating cash flow remained negative, approximately ₹91 crore. The June backlog includes substantial HAM and tariff-based projects; gross project cost is not all near-term EPC revenue. Funding commitments, concession assets and retained SPV exposure matter.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: reconcile consolidated cash conversion, new SPV equity commitments and net proceeds from asset recycling. Prefer an orderly base while the trend stays intact; do not buy merely because an order book is large.
invalidation: Downgrade if contract assets and financing needs outgrow execution, or completed-asset proceeds fail to replenish deployable cash.

thesis: Most interesting established business at a moderate historical earnings multiple; entry trend is weak.
new_evidence: Q1 EBITDA rose 26.5% with margin expansion to 12.81%, but revenue fell 4.6% and PAT grew only 0.8%. The presentation shows depreciation and interest rising sharply. Higher EBITDA has not yet become strong per-share earnings growth.
risk: The RBI private-cloud contract spans five years and includes infrastructure supply and support. FY26 cash conversion was incomplete; procurement, customer acceptance and collections can absorb funding. A large financial-institution customer is useful evidence of demand, not proof of high software-like margins.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: demonstrate RBI/NPCI billing and collections, sustained EPS improvement after depreciation/interest, and a fresh price base. A reclaim of the 50-session average would be an initial timing checkpoint, not sufficient by itself.
invalidation: Downgrade if margins improve only before depreciation/finance costs, or receivables and borrowing rise without EPS and cash improvement.

thesis: Best balance-sheet-led SME research candidate here; position liquidity is the binding constraint.
new_evidence: The Crisil rationale independently supports low gearing, adequate liquidity and an approximately ₹146 crore order book. It reports receivable days improving to 64 from 114. The voluntary Q1 update reports ₹34 crore invoicing and ₹25 crore bookings, explicitly unaudited and not subject to statutory review.
risk: ₹146 crore backlog is roughly one FY26 revenue year, not evidence of automatic doubling. FY26 OCF was approximately 40% of PAT in the audited statements. Cash equivalents and total bank/FD balances are different measures; not all deposits should be assumed freely available. Thin SME trading can frustrate exits.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: review the next audited/limited-review half-year, order conversion and cash collections. Verify revised award terms, SME lot size, circuits and an executable position size. Current 60-session median traded value is only about ₹0.30 crore/day.
invalidation: Downgrade if vendor advances/debtors rise disproportionately, bank guarantees constrain execution, or growth relies on repeated new funding.

thesis: The Citelum acquisition creates a better thesis than the original routine municipal order.
new_evidence: The acquisition opens city lighting/electrical infrastructure. Management targets ₹300–350 crore annual revenue from the vertical over three to four years, with about ₹100 crore planned investment. Those are targets and planned spending, not secured future earnings. Q1 revenue rose 11.65%, but EBITDA margin slipped from 6.61% to 6.32%.
risk: Growth currently exceeds profit growth. Acquisition economics, integration and public-sector collection remain open. FY26 cash conversion was weak relative to reported earnings. The price has now fallen below both major moving averages despite an apparently modest FY26 earnings valuation.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: obtain acquired revenue/profit, consideration, funding and a milestone budget. Track cash returns from the new vertical and a recovery in margins. Price recovery above approximately ₹601/₹634, the dated 200/50-session averages, is a checkpoint rather than an automatic order.
invalidation: Downgrade if the expansion consumes capital without cash earnings or acquisition-adjusted returns are poor.

thesis: Business-mix improvement is real, but headline profitability overstates what the full group earns.
new_evidence: The Q1 deck highlights ₹16 crore PAT EXCLUDING foundit. Its full consolidated table instead shows approximately ₹949 crore revenue, ₹21 crore EBITDA and a ₹2 crore PAT loss. STEAG contributes to growth, while foundit remains a meaningful drag. Both scopes must be tracked.
risk: New acquisition integration, financing costs and loss funding can consume operating improvements. Acquired revenue and renewals must be separated from organic incremental business. Do not apply the ex-foundit earnings multiple to the entire listed equity without accounting for the loss-making operation.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: positive full-group PAT and operating cash flow, declining foundit cash burn and evidence of accretive STEAG/LSG integration. The price trend is constructive, but a good chart alone does not close these financial gaps.
invalidation: Downgrade if profitable divisions repeatedly fund persistent losses or acquisition growth does not improve owner-attributable cash earnings.

thesis: Orders are converting into revenue, but earnings quality and entry timing still need work.
new_evidence: Q1 presentation revenue is approximately ₹853 crore, up 65%, and EBITDA margin 6.42%, versus 4.79% a year earlier. Closing backlog of ₹13,245 crore is slightly below FY26 close of ₹13,447 crore; Q1 inflow is ₹630 crore. This is backlog execution, not uninterrupted new-order acceleration.
risk: Strategic/group customer concentration and working-capital advances remain important. Presentation PAT treatment needs checking against primary results: the tabular PBT, tax, JV and OCI bridge yields about ₹18.34 crore before OCI, whereas the highlighted PAT line shows about ₹18.22 crore after OCI. Do not mix PAT with total comprehensive income.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: confirm primary-statement owner earnings, sustained margin recovery and collections as existing projects execute. Require a fresh base; price remains well below both 50/200-session averages.
invalidation: Downgrade if debtor/contract-asset growth outpaces funded execution or credit losses remain elevated.

thesis: Cheap sales valuation is insufficient while the latest quarter loses money.
new_evidence: The original Q1 consolidated statement shows revenue ₹755.08 crore, but group PAT loss ₹3.38 crore and parent-owner loss ₹3.59 crore. Strong sales do not establish profitable programme execution. FY26 group PAT and owner-attributable PAT also differ.
risk: Heavy capex, debt service, depreciation and price/cost pass-through can absorb the programme gains. Programme lifetime value should not be treated as one-year revenue. The price is below both major averages.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: customer price recovery, profitable production, cash flow after maintenance/growth capex and declining net debt. Wait for actual improvement rather than management guidance about freight normalisation.
invalidation: Downgrade if sales expand while funding and depreciation keep owner earnings depressed.

thesis: The Army contract is meaningful, but the delivery clock is conditional and the group is currently loss-making.
new_evidence: The contract states ₹563.35 crore INCLUDING taxes and duties, with delivery in tranches within twelve months FROM RELEASE OF ADVANCE PAYMENT after signing. It is not simply twelve months from the announcement. Q1 consolidated filings show revenue around ₹63 crore and a loss, rather than an established profitable ramp.
risk: Working-capital support, subsidiary economics and dilution require attention. Ownership of subsidiaries is not uniformly 100%; order revenue, full-group PAT and earnings attributable to listed shareholders are separate. Naval partnerships or licences should not be added as booked revenue.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: confirm advance receipt/date, procurement, accepted deliveries, billing, collection and the group margin bridge. Reassess fully diluted funding after warrants/allotments.
invalidation: Downgrade if advance/payment conditions slip, contract execution needs repeated equity funding or group losses persist as the order ramps.

call: Upgrade from blanket avoidance to speculative WATCH
thesis: Recent operating evidence deserves attention; it does not resolve valuation and shareholder-economics questions.
new_evidence: Q1 press material reports ₹374 crore revenue and ₹38 crore continuing-operation PAT. The actual consolidated statement reports about ₹35.41 crore total PAT, of which about ₹23.90 crore belongs to parent owners. An October order of approximately ₹174 crore has a stated Q2 2027 schedule. Distinguish these earnings scopes and the order from research partnerships.
risk: Do not use last year’s property/disposal-heavy PAT for recurring P/E. Reconcile acquisition financing, minorities and post-allotment shares. The database Q1 paid-capital fact is mis-scaled by 10,000× compared with the original ₹17,623.97 lakh statement, so automated current market cap is rejected.
upgrade_trigger: Before upgrading: bridge continuing PAT to owner PAT, acquisitions and fully diluted shares, then verify operating cash generation. The new order strengthens the operating thesis but does not justify buying at any price.
invalidation: Downgrade if the operating ramp does not reach parent shareholders, or acquisitions/working capital require opaque or repeated funding.

call: Avoid fresh entry at present; speculative watch only
thesis: A cheaper-looking quote has not removed valuation, cash-conversion or tender-stage risk.
new_evidence: The September filing confirms 958,166 rights shares at ₹950, taking equity shares to 19,044,784. At the 27 October close this implies approximately ₹1,928 crore equity value, around 14× FY26 consolidated revenue. The September CMSS announcement is an L1 position for over eight crore pieces, not a confirmed purchase order with a verified rupee profit contribution.
risk: The capacity ramp must be funded and converted into shipped, accepted, collected business. Rights proceeds are financing, not operating cash flow; the new equity base must be used in per-share analysis.
upgrade_trigger: Revisit after final awards, export shipment/collections, audited earnings/cash conversion and a valuation justified by sustainable owner earnings. Do not assign a value to the L1 quantity using an invented unit price.
invalidation: Downgrade further if tender access fails to turn into profitable collected revenue or expansion relies on repeated dilution.

call: Avoid fresh entry for this strategy
thesis: The restart is real, but headline PAT is not evidence of recurring profitability.
new_evidence: H1 FY27 shows revenue ₹99.46 crore, PBT loss ₹38.37 crore and PAT profit ₹524.78 crore. The primary statement and merger notes identify a ₹563.15 crore writeback of earlier tax provisions. The presentation also shows about ₹6,500 crore orders, execution extending to FY31 and ₹1,150 crore NaBFID financing.
risk: Treat the tax release as non-recurring, and use merger-restated comparatives. Financing is debt, not an award margin. Preference capital pending allotment and future funding matter to common shareholders. The operating cash-flow bridge also contains large balance-sheet releases, which should not be extrapolated as recurring shipbuilding cash.
upgrade_trigger: Revisit only after credible build/billing/collection milestones, contract-margin disclosure and a complete common-equity financing bridge. Do not calculate a recurring P/E from the tax-driven half-year PAT.
invalidation: Downgrade if restart spending/delivery delays consume financing before economically profitable vessels are delivered.
